issues.legal_issue: A landlord may rely on material alteration of rented accommodation or likely substantial diminution of its value as independent grounds for bringing an eviction suit without prior administrative permission.
material_facts: The landlord sued to evict a tenant who had carried out construction without the landlord’s written permission.
The lower courts found that the construction materially altered the accommodation, but the High Court found no determination that it had caused harm or damage or diminished the accommodation’s value.
issues.conclusion: The statutory grounds are alternatives: proof of material alteration alone is sufficient, even without proof that the alteration diminished or was likely to substantially diminish the accommodation’s value.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 3(1)(c) of the U.P. (Temporary) Control of Rent and Eviction Act, 1947, the ordinary meaning of “or” provides two independent grounds: construction that materially alters the accommodation, or construction likely substantially to diminish its value. A provision is ordinarily construed according to its language unless compelling reasons justify a different construction; no such reason supported reading “or” as “and.”

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_proceeding and tenant_made_unapproved_construction and (materially_altered_accommodation or likely_substantially_diminished_value)

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding to evict a tenant that is ordinarily subject to prior administrative permission.
predicates.tenant_made_unapproved_construction: The tenant made or permitted construction without the landlord’s written permission.
predicates.materially_altered_accommodation: The construction materially altered the rented accommodation.
predicates.likely_substantially_diminished_value: The construction was likely substantially to diminish the value of the rented accommodation.

issues.definition: If an eviction proceeding ordinarily requiring prior administrative permission involves unapproved tenant construction that either materially alters the accommodation or is likely substantially to diminish its value, the landlord may sue without that permission.

issues.legal_issue: Construction that materially changes the form or structure of rented accommodation is a material alteration even if it does not damage the premises or diminish their value.
material_facts: The tenant lowered the shop floor by excavating earth and installing a new floor.

The tenant correspondingly lowered the front door and cut away the plinthband on which it rested, lowered the staircase and added new steps, and lowered the exterior platform to match the new floor level.
The tenant made these changes without the landlord’s permission; the lower courts found them to be material alterations.
issues.conclusion: The changes altered the form and structure of the accommodation and were material alterations, regardless of whether they caused damage or diminished its value. The landlord was therefore entitled to maintain the eviction suit without prior administrative permission.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(1)(c) of the U.P. (Temporary) Control of Rent and Eviction Act, 1947, requires a fact-specific assessment of material alteration. In its ordinary meaning, material alterations are important changes that materially or substantially change the front or structure of the premises. Wates v. Rowland and Another and Blackmore v. Dimmer provide assistance in identifying structural alterations; Hyman v. Rose concerned a different question about a lease covenant and waste and did not govern this issue.

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding to evict a tenant that is ordinarily subject to prior administrative permission.
predicates.tenant_made_unapproved_construction: The tenant made or permitted construction without the landlord’s written permission.
predicates.construction_changed_form_or_structure: The construction materially changed the form or structure of the rented accommodation.

issues.definition: In an eviction proceeding ordinarily subject to prior administrative permission, unapproved tenant construction that changes the accommodation’s form or structure is a material alteration.
